name: OpenSSL
description: Toolkit for TLS and general-purpose cryptography.
summary: OpenSSL allows AI-assisted contributions, including substantial AI-written code and documentation, provided the contributor declares the tool and model with an Assisted-by trailer, has signed the newer CLA containing the AI clauses, and has personally read, tested and can defend the change. Trivial help such as single-line autocompletion, reformatting or spell-checking needs no declaration, and no submission without human review is accepted. AI-written issues and comments are not addressed.

evidence.quote: A non-trivial portion of a submission has been created with an AI tool when it has generated meaningful code, logic, or documentation — not merely assisted with trivial tasks like autocompletion of a single line, reformatting, or spell-checking.
This policy does not prohibit the use of AI tools. You are free to use whatever tools help you contribute effectively.
You are the author of everything you submit, whatever produced the first draft.

Similarly, if a non-trivial portion of a contribution was created using an AI tool, you must declare which agent and model were used, by adding `Assisted-by: {agent}:{model}` below the commit message:
Including AI-generated content in your contribution requires a signed CLA with the AI clauses (CLA v1.1 or later).
OpenSSL welcomes contributions from all developers, including those who use AI-assisted coding tools.
Add an Assisted-by trailer to your commit message in the format Assisted-by: {agent}:{model}, where {agent} is the tool or interface you used and {model} is the specific underlying model.
Always include the model name and version where known, so that the declaration is meaningful:
A commit may have more than one Assisted-by trailer if multiple tools were used.
Before submitting any contribution that includes non-trivial AI-generated content, you must have signed this new CLA.
Signing the old CLA is not sufficient for AI-assisted contributions, even if you have previously signed it.
The new CLA requires that you confirm you have the right to submit the AI-generated content and that you accept full responsibility for it.
You are responsible for everything you submit, whether or not AI helped write it.
Review all AI-generated code before submitting it. Do not submit output you have not read, understood and tested.
AI tools can produce plausible-looking but incorrect, insecure, or inefficient code.
Do not submit AI-generated code if you have reason to believe it reproduces third-party copyrighted material.
This policy does not permit submissions where no human has reviewed the content. AI tools may assist, but a human must direct the work, review the output, and be accountable for what is submitted.
Check for test coverage. AI-generated code must be accompanied by appropriate tests, just like any other contribution.
This policy applies to all public OpenSSL repositories, including all repositories under https://github.com/openssl.

A non-trivial portion of a submission has been created with an AI tool when it has generated meaningful code, logic, or documentation — not merely assisted with trivial tasks like autocompletion of a single line, reformatting, or spell-checking.
The `Assisted-by:` trailer (see below) discloses that a tool was used; it does not transfer responsibility for the result.
Security is critical to OpenSSL — AI-generated code must meet the same standards as any other contribution.
The OpenSSL project maintainers may reject or request revision of any submission, including AI-assisted ones, that does not meet project standards.
This policy does not create a lower bar for AI-assisted contributions.
